scope: Historical relationship, event-date and specimen-date reconciliation for the first audit response PR.
method: Read precise operative passages in statutes, commencement instruments, contemporary releases and audited reports.
Distinguish legal rename, corporate formation, asset transfer, cessation, dissolution, registry observation and branding.
Retain incompatible or less precise assertions with their provenance rather than inferring extra events.
Keep event dates, source publication dates, reporting periods, retrieval dates and logo adoption separate.

sources.title: British Columbia Enterprise Corporation Act, consolidation current to 25 November 1993
supports: BC Place Ltd., certificate 207097, was renamed British Columbia Enterprise Corporation with effect from 31 March 1987.
BCEC and B.C. Pavilion Corporation are named separately in section 2.
does_not_establish: BC Place Ltd. original incorporation date

sources.title: PavCo Service Plan 2004/05–2006/07
supports: Former B.C. Pavilion Corporation was incorporated on 3 May 1984.
PavCo was registered as a business name on 23 September 1999.

sources.title: BCEC financial statements, year ended 31 March 2003
sources.locator: Notes 1 (Nature of business) and 4 (Net assets transferred to shareholders)
supports: BCEC ceased operations on 30 September 1989 and remained inactive.
Certain assets and liabilities were transferred to the Province and, on shareholder instructions, PavCo on that day.
BCEC remained a separately reported corporation after 1989.
does_not_establish: A complete itemized schedule of transferred assets

sources.title: B.C. Pavilion Corporation audited financial statements, year ended 31 March 2025
sources.locator: Note 1, Authority and Nature of Operations
supports: Present PavCo was formed on 1 April 2008 by amalgamating former PavCo and Vancouver Convention Centre Expansion Project Ltd.
sources.caution: The web document title includes former BCEC; the audited note itself names former PavCo and VCCEP. Do not treat the catalogue title as evidence of a BCEC rename.

sources.title: B.C. Pavilion Corporation Act, SBC 2022 c.33
supports: Section 4 dissolves BCEC; sections 5 and 6 transfer its residual assets and liabilities to the government.
Section 10 requires commencement by regulation.
sources.caution: Royal assent on 3 November 2022 does not establish the dissolution date.

sources.title: B.C. Gazette Part II, B.C. Reg.71/2023, OIC171/2023
sources.locator: Approved and deposited 13 March 2023; operative paragraph (a)
supports: The entire B.C. Pavilion Corporation Act came into force on 13 March 2023.
sources.interpretation: Read with section 4 of the Act, this establishes BCEC statutory dissolution on 13 March 2023. The retained registry status entry dated 27 March is not substituted for commencement.

sources.title: British Columbia Enterprise Corporation Financial Restructuring Act, SBC 1987 c.39
sources.locator: Sections 1, 2 and 7; editorial note B.C. Reg.289/87
sources.review: Official statute text retrieved in search
supports: The Development Corporation’s property, assets, associated rights and liabilities were transferred to BCEC with effect from 31 March 1987.
sources.caution: The description of the BC Place/BCEC name lineage does not collapse all predecessor artwork into one exclusive line.

sources.title: CN closes BC Rail transaction, 14 July 2004
sources.locator: Release opening three paragraphs; SEC filing table of contents identifies release dated 14 July
sources.review: CN release filed with SEC read
supports: CN completed its BC Rail transaction on 14 July 2004 and announced step-by-step integration.
The interests acquired were BC Rail Ltd., BC Rail Partnership and operating rights over the roadbed.
sources.caution: The SEC filename contains jul1504 and the signature is dated 16 July. Neither is the stated closing date.

sources.title: CN 2004 audited financial statements, February 2005 filing
sources.locator: Note 3, Acquisitions, BC Rail; printed p. 11
supports: Acquisition completion and the beginning of phased operating integration are dated 14 July 2004.

sources.title: Province releases $1-billion investment partnership agreement, 12 August 2004
sources.locator: Opening agreement descriptions; paragraph beginning On July 2
supports: Formal closure occurred on 14 July 2004.
Shares and partnership units were transferred while the right-of-way, railbed and track remained publicly owned.

sources.title: British Columbia Public Accounts 2004/05
sources.locator: Printed p. 66, note 33, Significant Events: BCRC Operations
supports: The transaction was completed on 14 July 2004.
CN acquired the industrial freight railway business and assumed the Revitalization Agreement.
The infrastructure lease has an initial 60-year term with renewal provisions.
sources.caution: The operating business, statutory parent and infrastructure ownership are distinct.

sources.title: Transportation Safety Board railway investigation R05V0141
sources.review: Official search-index passage read; direct retrieval returned HTTP 403
supports: The TSB retrospectively dates CN’s acquisition of the BCR system to 15 July 2004.
does_not_establish: A separate next-day operational transfer distinct from the 14 July closing
sources.disposition: Preserve as an attributed retrospective date claim. Prefer the contemporary transaction releases and audited statements for the canonical closing date.

sources.title: BC Cancer history
supports: BC Cancer and the Foundation introduced an identity in 2017.
sources.caution: Year precision is retained in the original assertion.

sources.title: BC Cancer and BC Cancer Foundation strengthen partnership to break down cancer
sources.review: Official search-index announcement text read; direct retrieval returned HTTP 403
supports: The joint identity announcement was dated 15 November 2017.
BC Cancer Agency simplified its public name to BC Cancer.
does_not_establish: A merger of the Foundation and agency
sources.disposition: Explicit preferred_assertion decision selects the exact day and attaches the compatible year-only history as corroboration.

decisions.result: Remove the gallery continuation and BCEC becameId / PavCo predecessor claim. Preserve BC Place→BCEC rename and the typed 1989 asset-transfer event linking BCEC with PavCo.
decisions.limit: All three gallery collections remain separate; BC Development also contributes to BCEC history, so no exclusive one-to-one gallery lineage is inferred.

decisions.result: Keep 3 May 1984 predecessor incorporation and 1 April 2008 present-corporation amalgamation as distinct milestones.
Keep 30 September 1989 operating end, 13 March 2023 statutory dissolution and 27 March 2023 registry status entry distinct.
Use 14 July 2004 primary-source transaction date. Preserve previous Wikipedia assertion in superseded_assertion; relabel TSB 15 July evidence as a retrospective date claim.
Use an explicit reviewed preferred_assertion decision for this one event. Keep the year-only and exact-day originals.

The gallery accepts explicit ISO, year, fiscal-year, year-range, season/month and explicitly approximate date strings. It does not extract a year from descriptive sourceDate prose or observedDate. Both BC Housing records whose undated source discusses April 2019 become unknown-date specimens.
decisions.limit: Narrative sourceDate strings for other reports remain visible as contextual notes. They need reviewed structured specimenDate metadata before they can date a specimen; a report period or upload path alone is insufficient.

unresolved: Exact legal-versus-registry reason for the 1987 BCEC name-date difference was not established. Both observations are kept.
The timing reason for the 2023 registry status entry after statutory dissolution was not established.
The TSB July15 discrepancy is documented, not explained by an invented separate operational handover.
BC Cancer announcement and TSB live pages returned HTTP403; their official indexed passages were available and the access limitation is recorded.
This pass preserves BC Place’s previously recorded March25 1980 registry incorporation date; it did not independently refetch that registry record.
